purpose: Primary and authoritative sources for designing an established-meme template retrieval and ranking system.

sources.use: KYMKB template knowledge base, template semantics, retrieval and classification evidence
Reproducibility and available scraping and retrieval code
Semantic clustering of visually different templates from their caption usage
Template-independent communicative structures and model limitations
Hybrid semantic and similarity retrieval, current large-scale resource
Supervised template selection baseline and human evaluation design
Retrieval versus preference reranking and the limits of automated humor selection
Within-template pairwise preference learning and hierarchical intent reasoning
FAISS-based proof of concept and documented selection weaknesses
Large template pool, random-template baseline, and human meme evaluation dimensions
Pairwise judging, multiple perspectives, and ranking methodology; task is harmfulness rather than humor
Ontology, textual, visual, and structural meme search precedent
Historical evidence that semantic distinctiveness correlated with meme popularity in one platform dataset
Experimental evidence on processing fluency, coherence, and humor appreciation
Established renderable template inventory and box structure
Current volatile popularity and familiarity signal

notes: PDF-to-text outputs under raw/extracted are mechanical, unedited extractions of the preserved PDFs.
The meme-generation preprints are useful design evidence but are not treated as settled validation.
No source establishes a proven, general-purpose system for choosing the funniest template for a professional LinkedIn post.
